sections.label: Global e-commerce value and growth
sections.summary: Global e-commerce was estimated at US$26 trillion in 2018, and retail e-commerce grew 37% in the first half of 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In 2018, the value of global e-commerce was estimated at US$26 trillion, equivalent to 30% of the global GDP that year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 pandemic has given further boost to global retail e-commerce, which grew by 37% in the first half of 2020, more than double the rate in 2019.

sections.label: Clause 6 adopts MLETR
sections.summary: Clause 6 introduces a new part 2A to adopt the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records with modifications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill introduces a new part 2A to adopt the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records, or MLETR, with certain modifications.

sections.label: Electronic bill of lading equivalence
sections.summary: Clause 6 enables an electronic bill of lading legally equivalent to a paper bill of lading, effective beyond contractual framework parties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill addresses this gap by enabling the creation and use of an electronic bill of lading that is legally equivalent to a paper bill of lading which will be legally effective beyond parties to such a contractual framework.

sections.label: Savings from electronic bills of lading
sections.summary: The Digital Container Shipping Association estimates about US$4 billion saved annually if half of container shipping lines adopt electronic bills of lading.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Digital Container Shipping Association estimates that about US$4 billion would be saved annually if just half of today's container shipping lines adopt electronic bills of lading.

sections.label: Timely legal infrastructure for ETRs
sections.summary: The Bill provides enabling legal infrastructure for creating and using ETRs under the law in a trusted and secure manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: With such technological solutions available today, it is timely to provide the enabling legal infrastructure through this Bill to allow the creation and use of ETRs under the law in a trusted and secure manner.

sections.label: Singapore first for ETRs framework
sections.summary: Singapore will be one of the first countries to enact a legislative framework for ETRs based on the MLETR.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: With these amendments, Singapore will be one of the first countries to enact a legislative framework for ETRs based on the MLETR, the Model Law, giving a competitive edge to our key industries like shipping, and reinforcing our status as a leading maritime and trade hub.

sections.label: Promoting cross-border electronic transferable records
sections.summary: New section 16P supports non-discrimination against foreign origin or use of ETRs to facilitate cross-border use.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Given the tangible benefits to global trade, we will continue to work with our international partners to promote the adoption of the MLETR through our free trade agreements and digital economy agreements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In this bid to promote cross-border transactions, the new section 16P will facilitate the cross-border use of ETRs by supporting the principle of non-discrimination against the foreign origin or use of an ETR.

sections.label: Change of medium and technology neutrality
sections.summary: New sections 16M and 16N enable change of medium between physical documents and ETRs without affecting parties' rights.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Recognising that not every country would have enacted the MLETR, the new sections 16M and 16N contain substantive provisions that enable the change of medium from a physical transferable document or instrument, to an ETR and vice versa.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: A change of medium in accordance with the provisions of the Bill does not affect the rights and obligations of the parties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Consistent with the MLETR the amendments introduced by the Bill abide by the principle of technology neutrality, which means that legislation should not impose the use of, or otherwise favour, any specific technology.

sections.label: Cost savings from digitalising bills of lading
sections.summary: Digital Container Shipping Association predicted potential cost savings of more than $4 billion a year for maritime industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: A recent finding from the Digital Container Shipping Association predicted a potential cost savings of more than $4 billion a year on the maritime industry by digitalising the paper-based bills of lading.

sections.label: Paper elimination and registration numbers
sections.summary: Digitalisation could eliminate over 7,800 tonnes of paper annually; 2019 registrations were 24,488, double 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Apart from the clear cost saving benefit, digitalisation could help eliminate more than 7,800 tonnes of paper documents annually, which is equivalent to 80 Boeing 747 planes filled with paper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In 2019, the number of registrations reported was 24,488 and this doubled, the registration numbers, in 2017.

sections.label: Priority for high-volume transactions
sections.summary: Member asks Government and Ministry to prioritise large volume transactions like option-to-purchase agreements for convenience and cost savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I know that Minister has shared this in his speech earlier, that the Ministry will be looking into this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And I would like to ask the the Government and the Ministry to give priority consideration where there are large volume transactions happening on a day-to-day basis, including for example, option-to-purchase agreements, so that it will be much more convenient and save time and cost for our normal ordinary citizens.

sections.label: MTI plans for blockchain platforms
sections.summary: Member asks status of MTI's plans on blockchain platforms for transferable electronic transactions and whether one platform is favoured.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Minister Iswaran did explicitly point to these issues but MTI's position on incorporating such innovations, insofar as the amended law is concerned, remains somewhat unclear.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It therefore behooves me to ask what the status of MTI's plans are on the roll-out of these blockchain based platforms for transferable electronic transactions in this space, such as, cargo access, smart bill of lading or the International Port Community System Association or IPCSA's e-bill of lading initiative, which I believe Minister Iswaran also alluded to.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And it would be helpful to know if MTI has already decided on favouring one of these platforms versus another, and if relevant industry players have been informed.

sections.label: SMEs and electronic trade records
sections.summary: The amendments do not include provisions supporting SMEs in adopting trade-related electronic transactions records, and the speaker urges embedding trade elements into Enterprise SG programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The amendments as they stand do not include provisions that will support our SMEs in adopting trade-related electronic transactions records, thereby transitioning to this 21st century economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps this issue will be addressed in subsidiary legislation or is implicit in the number of existing policies to support digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But I believe it is worth reiterating the importance of embedding the trade elements outlined in this Bill into programmes such as Enterprise SG's Enterprise Development Grant or Productivity Solutions Grant.

sections.label: Registered Lasting Powers of Attorney
sections.summary: As of August 2020, there were 93,000 registered LPAs, with only about 30% of the 60-69 age group registering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As of August 2020, there are just 93,000 registered LPAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Only about 30% of the 60-69 year-old age group registered for an LPA.

sections.label: UNCITRAL Model Law adoption
sections.summary: The UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records has only been adopted by Bahrain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The reality, as the Minister pointed out, is that the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records has only been adopted by Bahrain.

sections.label: Enforceability of electronically signed deeds
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify whether deeds signed using electronic signatures, complying with all other formalities, are enforceable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister clarify if deeds signed using electronic signatures, which comply with all other formalities required for deeds, are enforceable?

sections.label: Digitalised trade documents legal recognition
sections.summary: Documentation and processing can be up to 20% of shipping cost, and legal recognition for digitalised trade documents will cut costs, speed processing and boost efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As a result, the documentation and processing work can constitute up to 20% of the cost of shipping the goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Providing legal recognition for digitalised trade documents, such as bills of lading, negotiable instruments, documents of title, bills of exchange, promissory notes, consignment notes and warehouse receipts will cut administrative costs, speed up processing time and boost efficiency.

sections.label: Digital Lasting Power of Attorney recognition
sections.summary: The proposed ETA changes seek legal recognition for digital forms of the Lasting Power of Attorney, pending readiness of the Mental Capacity Act and administrative framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, the proposed changes to the ETA also seek to provide legal recognition for digital forms of the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), pending the readiness of the related legislation, the Mental Capacity Act, and supporting administrative framework.

sections.label: Power of attorney digitalisation scope
sections.summary: The Bill amends the ETA to bring power of attorney into scope when frameworks are ready, paving the way for digitalising the Lasting Power of Attorney.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, the other area not covered under the ETA is the creation, performance or enforcement of an indenture, declaration of trust or power of attorney.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill seeks to introduce changes to bring the power of attorney into its scope when the relevant legislative framework and administrative structure are ready, paving the way for the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) to be digitalised.

sections.label: ETA amendment and trade documents
sections.summary: The Bill amends the ETA, adopts the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records, and deletes Item 2 covering trade documents from the First Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill is one of the many steps that Singapore is taking in its journey to digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill seeks to amend the ETA and adopt with modifications the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This amendment specifically deletes Item 2 from the First Schedule of the ETA which are trade documents such as negotiable instruments, documents of title and bills of lading.

sections.label: MSF consultation on LPA digitalisation
sections.summary: MSF's 2020 public consultation considered digitalising LPAs, reducing the time needed from three weeks to eight working days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: MSF in its public consultation in 2020 has considered the potential digitalisation of LPAs; reducing the time needed from three weeks to just eight working days.

sections.label: Timeframe for LPA and wills digitalisation
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for announcements on the estimated timeframe for deleting other First Schedule items, particularly those on digitalising LPAs and wills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This hopefully will bring about a higher take-up rate of LPAs and wills, and reduce the risks of litigation and disputes on competing LPAs and wills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I would ask the Minister if there can be further announcements on the estimated timeframe for the deletion of the other items in the First Schedule, particularly those relating to the electronic or digitalisation of LPAs and wills.

sections.label: COVID-19 business digitalisation survey findings
sections.summary: Speakers said COVID-19 accelerated business digitalisation by two to five years and tripled e-commerce; an SBF survey found 39% of companies increased IT budgets and 58% cited high investment cost as a barrier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the business front, COVID-19 has accelerated business digitalisation efforts across industries by almost two to five years and e-commerce trade have tripled, according to speakers at last week’s World Economic Forum's Davos Agenda.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a recent National Business Survey 2020/2021 conducted by the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) from 9 October to 28 November 2020 with respondents from 1,075 companies across key industries – 85% from SMEs and 15% from large companies – it was found that 39% of companies report that their IT/digitalisation budgets have increased as a result of the COVID-19 situation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the same survey, 58% of the businesses highlighted that the key barrier to digitalisation is the perceived high investment cost of technology adoption.

sections.label: Singapore SME digital maturity scores
sections.summary: Based on IMDA's Digital Acceleration Index 2020, most Singapore SMEs have very low digital maturity scores, with 67% being Digital Starters at the bottom.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just to complete the backdrop of where all the SMEs in Singapore stand, based on IMDA's Digital Acceleration Index 2020, most Singapore SMEs have very low digital maturity scores, with 67% of SMEs being Digital Starters – at the bottom.

sections.label: Digital trade agreements and Bill
sections.summary: Singapore's leadership with TradeTrust, Digital Economy Agreements and the Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Bill will accelerate digital trade safely and plug Singapore companies into global trade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore’s leadership with TradeTrust, the Digital Economy Agreements with Chile, New Zealand and Australia, and now this Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Bill will pave the way for accelerating digital trade safely with open transparent standards, for Singapore companies and give us a leg-up in being plugged into the global trade eco-system.

sections.label: SMEs and digital trade platform
sections.summary: Most SMEs are Digital Starters facing cost and skills barriers, so one suggestion is a government or sector-funded national digital trade platform, like PayNow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sixty-seven percent of SMEs are Digital Starters, and they are still battling with the barriers of investment cost, skills, management expertise and so on, to get across the digital chasm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Specific to the preparation of our businesses especially the SMES for the adoption of Electronic Transactions, I believe we need to bear in mind that there will be increased costs in the short to mid term, when there are investments required, and there is a time when both manual and digital will have to co-exist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, one suggestion to consider is that the platform for digital trade to be part of a national infrastructure funded/sponsored by Government, PPP or some sectoral Queen Bee, pretty much like how the banks effectively bank-rolled PayNow to facilitate e-payment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: PayNow Corporate has crossed more than 4 million registrations in December, of course, accelerated by COVID-19, no doubt.

sections.label: Trade document processing costs
sections.summary: Maersk and IBM research shows processing trade documents can cost up to 20% of a shipment's physical transportation cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To give some sense of proportion, according to research done by Maersk and IBM, and as highlighted by Mr Don Wee, the cost of processing trade documents could cost as much as 20% of the physical transportation cost of a shipment of goods, which is quite staggering if you think about it.

sections.label: Consent for electronic transferable records
sections.summary: The ETA amendments do not mandate electronic transferable records; new section 16D requires both parties to consent, so businesses may choose.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the ETA do not mandate the use of ETRs but they are an important enabler that confer greater certainty to the business environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The new section 16D provides that both parties must consent to the use of the ETR and, therefore, businesses are free to choose.

sections.label: IMDA TradeTrust digital utility
sections.summary: IMDA's TradeTrust is a digital utility with globally accepted standards and frameworks connecting governments and businesses to a neutral public blockchain.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: One such example is IMDA's TradeTrust, a digital utility that comprises globally accepted standards and frameworks that connects Governments and businesses to a neutral and public blockchain.

sections.label: Rotterdam electronic bills of lading proof
sections.summary: Collaboration with the Port of Rotterdam produced a technical Proof of Concept transferring title for electronic bills of lading between two standalone TradeTrust solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our collaboration with the Port of Rotterdam culminated in the successful technical Proof of Concept where transfers of title for electronic bills of lading were achieved between two standalone solutions on the TradeTrust framework.

sections.label: TradeTrust free open source licensing
sections.summary: The TradeTrust software is distributed for free under open source licensing terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The TradeTrust software is distributed for free under open source licensing terms.

sections.label: New sections 16F to 16I requirements
sections.summary: New sections 16F to 16I set out requirements an electronic record must meet to be recognised under the ETA as equivalent to a paper transferable document or instrument.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I mentioned before, the new sections 16F to 16I set out specific requirements that an electronic record must meet in order to be recognised under the ETA as being a functional equivalent of a paper transferable document or instrument.

sections.label: New section 16G electronic signatures
sections.summary: With new section 16G, the ETA can now legally recognise electronic signatures for transferable documents or instruments.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: With the new section 16G, it is now possible to rely on the ETA to legally recognise electronic signatures for transferable documents or instruments.

sections.label: Studying removal of Exclusion List items
sections.summary: The Government is studying progressively removing remaining documents and instruments from the Exclusion List, seeking to remove as many exclusions as possible by 2023, with no specific estimated time of arrival.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Looking ahead, the Government is studying the feasibility of progressively removing the remaining documents and instruments from the Exclusion List, and we will be guided by the benefits that will accrue to citizens, if they are made available in electronic form whilst keeping a keen eye on the safeguards that are necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To Mr Zhulkarnain's specific point, we do not have a specific estimated time of arrival for the Electronic Transactions Act's Exclusion List to be reduced or removed completely.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But as a general move as part of the Government's larger effort, we are seeking to remove as many of these exclusions as possible by 2023.

sections.label: Digitalising LPAs registration time
sections.summary: Excluding the mandatory three-week waiting period, digitalising LPAs could cut registration time from an average of three weeks to about eight working days.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Excluding the mandatory three-week waiting period, as some Members have observed, digitalising LPAs could cut the time needed to register LPAs from an average of three weeks to about eight working days.

sections.label: New section 16D consent requirement
sections.summary: New section 16D provides that both contracting parties must consent to the use of ETRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The new section 16D specifically provides that both contracting parties must consent to the use of ETRs.

sections.label: Digitalisation skills and support steps
sections.summary: The passage states steps were taken to give companies and individuals digitalisation knowledge and skills, citing the Digital Resilience Bonus and SG Digital Office Community Hubs, and calls the Bill an important step for the trade sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Hence, we have taken additional steps to ensure that companies and individuals have the knowledge and skills to embrace digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I can give you a long list but it would suffice to illustrate with one or two, for example, the Digital Resilience Bonus which was aimed at the retail and food services sector, and our more recent SG Digital Office Community Hubs which ensure that we reach out to segments of Singaporeans who may require more support in their digitalisation journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: However, the landscape is ever-changing and we need to be agile to adopt new technologies and to respond to changing circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This Bill is an important step for the digitalisation of our trade sector.

sections.label: Reviewing other sectors for digital economy
sections.summary: The Government will progressively review other sectors, guided by benefits to people and businesses, safeguards to preserve trust, and Singapore's competitive position in the global digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Government will progressively review these other sectors, focused and guided by the benefits they bring to our people and businesses the safeguards that are necessary to preserve trust and, ultimately, to secure Singapore's competitive position in the global digital economy.
